title: Converting fractions, decimals and percents
blurb: Switch any value between fraction, decimal and percent form quickly and without decimal-point slips.
question: A pharmacy label lists a cream as 2.5% hydrocortisone, and the pharmacist asks you to record the strength as a decimal and as a fraction in lowest terms. What do you write?

teach.body: Formally, a fraction a/b means a ÷ b, a decimal writes that value in place-value form, and a percent means "per hundred" (45% = 45/100). In plain English: 3/4, 0.75 and 75% are the same amount wearing three different outfits. The HESI A2 asks you to switch outfits fast, so learn one rule for each switch and a short list of benchmark values you never have to work out.

Rule
Example
teach.caption: Simplify a fraction by dividing top and bottom by their greatest common factor (GCF).

teach.h: Worked example: 3/8 as a decimal and a percent
items: Fraction to decimal: numerator ÷ denominator, so 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375.
Decimal to percent: multiply by 100 (move the point 2 places right): 0.375 → 37.5%.
Check 2: 3/8 is a little under 1/2 (50%), and 37.5% is a little under 50%. Reasonable.

teach.caption: Fill empty places with zeros as the point moves: 7% → 0.07, never 0.7.

teach.h: Worked example: percent and decimal to a fraction
items: 0.125 → the last digit sits in the thousandths place, so 0.125 = 125/1000.

head: Fraction
Decimal

teach.caption: Eighths go up in steps of 0.125 (12.5%); fifths go up in steps of 0.2 (20%).
Thirds and sixths never end as decimals. Exact answers use the fraction or the mixed-number percent.

teach.text: The decimal point moves TWO places, in the right direction. 0.04 is 4%: not 40% (point moved three places) and not 0.4% (point moved one place). And 0.5% is 0.005: a percent smaller than 1 becomes a decimal smaller than 0.01.

teach.h: Scenario: Jordan reads a pharmacy label
teach.body: Jordan Reyes, a nursing applicant working as a pharmacy technician, sees a cream labeled 2.5% hydrocortisone. Decimal: 2.5 ÷ 100 = 0.025 (point 2 places left). Fraction: 0.025 ends in the thousandths place, so 25/1000; the GCF of 25 and 1000 is 25, giving 1/40. Check: 1 ÷ 40 = 0.025 and 0.025 × 100 = 2.5%. Jordan records 0.025 and 1/40.

teach.text: Two more classic slips: dividing the denominator by the numerator (3/8 → 8 ÷ 3 = 2.67, which is more than 1 and cannot equal a proper fraction) and writing a percent over 10 instead of 100 (35% → 35/10).

items: Decimal ↔ percent: move the point 2 places (right to get a percent, left to get a decimal).
Percent → fraction: over 100, then simplify by the GCF; decimal → fraction: use the place value.
Know the benchmarks (eighths, fifths, thirds) so you can spot answers instantly.
Check every conversion by converting back.

summary: You can now convert any non-negative value between fraction, decimal and percent form, simplify the fraction to lowest terms, and check your answer by converting back. You also know the benchmark values and the decimal-point slips the HESI A2 uses as wrong answers.

whyNot.0: The decimal point moved only 1 place: 0.4375 × 10 = 4.375, not × 100.
whyNot.1: This divides the denominator by the numerator: 16 ÷ 7 ≈ 2.2857, which is greater than 1.
whyNot.3: This attaches a percent sign to the decimal without multiplying by 100.

A.q: A clinic reports that 0.6% of patients had a reaction to a vaccine. Which decimal is equal to 0.6%?
A.why: Percent to decimal: divide by 100, moving the point 2 places left. 0.6 → 0.06 → 0.006.

whyNot.1: 0.06 is the point moved only 1 place; 0.06 equals 6%, ten times too big.
whyNot.2: 0.6 just drops the percent sign; 0.6 equals 60%.
whyNot.3: 0.0006 moves the point 3 places; that equals 0.06%.

A.q: Express 0.36 as a fraction in lowest terms.
A.why: The 6 is in the hundredths place, so 0.36 = 36/100. The GCF of 36 and 100 is 4: 36/100 = 9/25. Check: 9 ÷ 25 = 0.36.

whyNot.0: 18/50 equals 0.36 but is not in lowest terms: 18 and 50 still share a factor of 2.
whyNot.1: 9/20 = 0.45. Dividing 36 by 4 but 100 by 5 changes the value.
whyNot.2: 36/10 = 3.6. The last digit is in the hundredths place, so the denominator is 100.

B.q: A recipe calls for 2 3/4 cups of oats. Which percent is equal to 2 3/4?
B.why: 2 3/4 = 2 + 0.75 = 2.75. Multiply by 100: 275%. A value greater than 1 is always more than 100%.

whyNot.0: 27.5% moves the point only 1 place: 2.75 × 10, not × 100.
whyNot.2: 234% reads the digits of the mixed number as a decimal (2.34), which is not 2 3/4.
whyNot.3: 575% comes from treating 2 3/4 as 23/4 = 5.75, misreading the whole number as a tens digit.

B.q: Which pair shows two forms that are both equal to 0.065?
B.why: 0.065 × 100 = 6.5%. As a fraction, 0.065 = 65/1000; divide by the GCF 5 to get 13/200. Check: 13 ÷ 200 = 0.065.

whyNot.0: Both forms equal 0.65, ten times too big: 65% and 13/20 = 0.65.
whyNot.2: 13/200 is right, but 0.65% = 0.0065, which moves the point one place too far.

B.q: Of 40 patients seen at a walk-in clinic on Monday, 3 needed stitches. What percent of the patients needed stitches?

whyNot.1: 75% is ten times too big; 75% of 40 would be 30 patients.
whyNot.2: 0.75% moves the point only 1 place from 0.075, and it would mean 0.3 of a patient.
whyNot.3: 0.075% attaches a percent sign to the decimal without multiplying by 100.

C.q: Which value is NOT equivalent to 3/8?
C.why: 3/8 = 0.375 = 37.5%. 3.75% = 0.0375, which is one tenth of 3/8, so it is not equivalent.

whyNot.0: 375/1000 = 0.375, the same value as 3/8 (it simplifies by 125 to 3/8).

C.q: An IV bag is labeled 0.9% sodium chloride. Which fraction in lowest terms equals 0.9%?
C.why: 0.9% = 0.9 ÷ 100 = 0.009. The 9 sits in the thousandths place: 9/1000, already in lowest terms. Check: 9 ÷ 1000 = 0.009 = 0.9%.

whyNot.2: 9/10 = 0.9 = 90%: it drops the percent sign instead of dividing by 100.

C.q: Tamika answered 42 of 48 pharmacology quiz questions correctly. What percent did she score?

whyNot.0: 114.3% divides 48 by 42; a score cannot be more than 100% of the questions.
whyNot.1: 8.75% moves the point only 1 place from 0.875.
whyNot.2: 0.875% attaches the percent sign without multiplying by 100.

reteach.title: Think in dollars and cents
reteach.question: A dollar is 100 cents, and percent means "per hundred." If every value is a share of one dollar, how do fractions, decimals and percents line up?

blocks.h: Percent is cents out of a dollar
blocks.body: A quarter is 1/4 of a dollar. In decimal dollars it is $0.25, and it is 25 cents, which is 25 out of 100: 25%. The decimal tells you dollars, the percent tells you cents. So to turn a decimal into a percent, ask "how many cents?": $0.08 is 8 cents, 8%. And half a cent ($0.005) is 0.5%, a percent smaller than 1.

blocks.text: A nickel is $0.05, five cents, 5%: not 50%. Count the cents and the zero after the point stays put.

explain.body: Divide the numerator (top) by the denominator (bottom). A proper fraction (top smaller than bottom) always gives a decimal between 0 and 1, which is a quick check that you divided the right way round.

test.q: A bottle of saline is 5/8 full. Which decimal shows how full it is?

whyNot.0: 0.0625 = 1/16; the decimal point has slipped one place left.
whyNot.1: 1.6 is 8 ÷ 5, the denominator divided by the numerator; a proper fraction must be less than 1.
whyNot.3: 6.25 has the point one place too far right.

explain.body: Multiply by 100 to go from decimal to percent (point 2 places right). Divide by 100 to go from percent to decimal (point 2 places left). A percent over 100 gives a decimal over 1: 250% = 2.5.

test.q: A patient's fluid intake was 125% of the target. Which decimal is equal to 125%?

whyNot.0: 12.5 moves the point only 1 place left.
whyNot.2: 0.125 moves the point 3 places left; that is 12.5%.
whyNot.3: 125 drops the percent sign without dividing by 100; that is 12,500%.

explain.body: For a decimal, the place value of the last digit is the denominator: 0.45 = 45/100. For a percent, write it over 100. Then divide top and bottom by the greatest common factor until no factor is shared.

test.q: Write 0.45 as a fraction in lowest terms.
test.why: 0.45 = 45/100. Divide top and bottom by the GCF, 5: 9/20. Check: 9 ÷ 20 = 0.45.

whyNot.0: 45/100 is equal to 0.45 but not in lowest terms; 45 and 100 share a factor of 5.
whyNot.1: 45/10 = 4.5; the last digit is in the hundredths place, so the denominator is 100.
whyNot.2: 9/25 = 0.36; the top was divided by 5 but the bottom by 4.

explain.body: Know eighths, fifths, quarters and thirds instantly. Thirds and sixths repeat: 1/3 = 0.333... = 33 1/3%, so 0.3 and 30% are only approximations, never equal.

test.q: Which value is NOT equal to 1/3?

whyNot.1: 0.333... with the 3 repeating forever is exactly 1/3.
